verdicts.evidence: Cursor's refusal reports `stream: ""` instead of `"stdout"`. The only reader, gate-hook's command, writes to stderr when `stream === "stderr"` and to stdout otherwise, so the text still lands on stdout with exit 0. Measured: the direct return value differs (648 of 4,545 cases, the stream field only) and `gate-hook --harness cursor` on the eleven probe missions is byte-identical on stdout, stderr and exit. Survived the CI unit pass on this branch and the whole-net pass of 2026-09-29 (scripts/mutation-wholenet.mjs, seven legs, serial). Measurement: identical on all 11 missions × 11 commands (121 runs); 648 of 4545 direct calls differ. Probe suite 2026-09-28 (scratch recipe, reproduced in the PR): eleven missions built with the pristine 0.42.3-dev build — `init` (blank), `init --example`, and the example with a dead pointer, the regulated tier on, a drifted seal, an edited and a removed rule, a failing after-hook, no scaffold-lock (unrecorded corpus), an under-filled framing note, a DRAFT ADR, and a fresh mission with two agent ratifications. Each mutant was spliced alone into dist/lib and eleven commands were run on each mission (check with and without --strict, --json, --sarif, --hooks; gate-hook for claude, cursor and gemini), exit code, stdout and stderr compared byte for byte with the pristine build. Positive control: the killed mutants gate-hook L77 and sarif L161 applied the same way differ on the regulated mission.
